description: paintOf(machine, now) — how a machine is DRAWN, as opposed to how it is filtered. statusOf() collapses an aged report to 'stale' for the filters and the counts; painting keeps the hue and marks it faded instead, so the map says what the machine last was without claiming it is that now. The two share one threshold: faded is true on exactly the inputs where statusOf returns 'stale' *and* a report exists. A machine with no reports at all has no hue to fade — it paints as tone 'stale', faded false, and that is the only thing grey now means. Each case also carries expectedLatestAt: the timestamp of latest(machine), which is what the sheet stamps beside the relative time.

paintCases.description: Nobody has ever reported this machine: there is no colour to wash out, so it paints grey at full strength.
A report filed at the current instant paints its own colour, unfaded.
A report exactly staleAfterMs old is still current — same side of the boundary statusOf takes ('> staleAfterMs', not '>='), so the two can never disagree about one machine.
1ms past 18h. statusOf() says 'stale'; paintOf() keeps tone 'ok' and sets faded. This is the whole change: the pin does not go grey, it goes pale green.
However old the report gets, the hue is kept and faded stays true — there is no second, harsher decay step.
Same rule as statusOf: the last element of reports decides both the tone and the timestamp, whatever came before it.
reports is ordered, not sorted by the reader: an aged last element fades even when an earlier entry is newer. Guards a port that reaches for max(at) instead of last().
